method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase with exact formula, macro, identifier and list-structure comparison. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Four coding capabilities common to computation models, numerical indices, computation records, and primitive-recursive decoding claims.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Every computation model allows systematic descriptions of computable-function definitions; complete run records for a fixed input; checks that a claimed record really is a terminating run of the given definition on that input; and extraction of the output value from a complete run record.
samples.checks: The four operations, Turing-machine configuration example, definedness/halting qualification and final-tape example all remain in their original order.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A computable function description has a numerical index from which its instructions can be computed; a complete run is coded by one number. The arithmetic relation saying s codes the run of program e on input x and the output function for code s are computable, indeed primitive recursive. These facts yield model-independent computability results.
samples.checks: The direction of recovery from the index, the roles of e/x/s, the stronger primitive-recursive claim for both objects and model independence are preserved.

source_observations: T067 supports the established coding family and T321 the index word, but the full computation-record formulation is controlled by the frozen OpenLogic source.
The source's 'record' is a complete halting computation record for the test and output claims; the translation keeps that qualification.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
No TeX reader build was run for this source-only unit checkpoint.
